title: How is MDX compiled, and which components may a stage document execute?
statement: Stage documents under `planning-content/stages/` are agent-authored content. MDX compiles to executable JavaScript, so the compilation strategy must state which components a document may reference and what happens to a reference outside that set.
notes: ⚠️ The load-bearing property is that agent-authored content must NOT implicitly become arbitrary application code. This project's whole discipline is that content is data the tool reads (#88 forbids authoring artifacts by hand precisely so the writer is a typed operation) — a document format whose default is 'anything in scope is callable' inverts that. The answer needs three parts: where compilation happens, the allowlist of components a document may use, and the behaviour on an unknown reference (refuse, or render inert). Refusing is consistent with how `checkJob` treats a shell-string command: refused rather than sanitised, because sanitising means guessing what the author meant. ⚠️ PRIMARY-DOCUMENT PASS 2026-08-26 (AST-0023, AST-0024, AST-0025; EVD-0025..EVD-0033, every claim quote-verified). STILL UNANSWERED, and deliberately so — search-backed discovery of failure reports and operational constraints has not been possible, and those could change the component-boundary decision. ⚠️ WHAT THE DOCUMENTATION SETTLES. Part 1 — compilation happens in the bundler through `@next/mdx`, and a root `mdx-components` file is mandatory. Part 2 — THE PREMISE IS WRONG: there is no allowlist to configure. MDX documents may import ESM and contain whole JavaScript programs, and the component mapping substitutes rather than restricts. Part 3 — an unresolved reference throws at runtime, which is a diagnostic for a mistaken author and not a boundary against a capable one. ⚠️ WHAT IS LEFT IS A PRODUCT JUDGEMENT, NOT A RESEARCH GAP. MDX's own position is that safety rests on trusting the author. So the question becomes whether agent-authored stage documents are trusted code — and #88 forbids hand-authoring artifacts precisely because the writer should be a typed operation. Reading more documentation will not settle that. ⚠️ WHAT SEARCH IS STILL OWED, and why it is worth waiting for: whether anyone has run agent-authored or otherwise semi-trusted MDX in production and what went wrong; whether restricting the compiler (rejecting ESM and expression nodes via a plugin) is something projects actually do or something that breaks in practice; and the operational cost of the alternative — compiling stage documents as plain markdown and rendering MDX only for a fixed set of authored pages. Those are failure reports, not specifications, and direct retrieval cannot find them. ⚠️ IT ALSO CONSTRAINS AND IS CONSTRAINED BY REQ-0021. If a document may reference components, the permitted set is another surface a direct planning-content read could enter through, so static confinement has to cover it. ⚠️ AND NOTHING HERE SETTLES CACHE COMPONENTS: DEC-0019 was chosen so the read contract holds with that flag either way, and no finding above touches it.
